name: Yamaha YZF-R1 cross-plane inline-four, 2009-2014 generation (model code 14B, 998 cc, 78.0 x 52.2 mm; data is for the 2009 model year)
summary: An inline-four whose crank pins sit 90 degrees apart, so it fires at uneven 270-180-90-180 degree intervals instead of an even 180; the result is a loping, V4-like growl rather than the usual inline-four scream. On the 2009 bike it exits through a 4-2-1-2 titanium system with an EXUP valve and twin under-seat mufflers.

cylinders.note: 'new 1,000cc liquid-cooled, in-line 4-cylinder, 4-valve DOHC engine with a crossplane crankshaft'

layout.note: Transverse inline four. Yamaha's spec table calls it 'Forward-inclined parallel 4-cylinder'.

bore_mm.note: Yamaha news release, 2009 European model: 'largest bore ever for a Yamaha 1,000cc supersport model at 78 x 52.2 mm'. 2009 service manual gives cylinder bore 78.000-78.010 mm (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1080239/Yamaha-2009-Yzf-R1-Y.html?page=42).

stroke_mm.note: Same sentence as bore. The 2009 racing kit manual's STK (stock-class) column prints 78.0 x 52.5 mm, apparently a misprint; its STD column prints 78.0 x 52.2 (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/805484/Yamaha-Yzf-R1.html?page=5).

displacement_cc.note: Spec table: 998 cm3. Service manual prints 998.0 cm3.

rod_length_mm.note: Not found. The 2009 service manual's connecting-rod section gives only bearing clearances (crankshaft-pin-to-big-end-bearing clearance 0.034-0.058 mm) and no centre-to-centre length; vendor listings found gave no figure for this generation. Do not reuse the 1998-2003 R1 figure (110.5 mm) seen on vendor pages; it is a different engine.

firing_order.note: Quote: 'A traditional in-line 4 cylinder's firing order is normally 1,2,4,3 with a 180 degree interval. This new R1 engine fires 1,3,2,4 cylinders and the firing intervals are uneven at 270 / 180/ 90 /180 degrees.' The page is totalmotorcycle.com reproducing Yamaha's 2009 model feature copy (Yamaha Canada/USA text), not a Yamaha-hosted page. Cylinder numbering convention (which side is cylinder 1) is NOT stated on any page opened; Yamaha practice is to number from the rider's left, but that is unsourced here.

crank.value: Cross-plane: four crank pins on two planes at right angles, each pin 90 degrees from its neighbour. Pin angles by cylinder 1-2-3-4: 0, 90, 270, 180 degrees (inner pair at right angles to the outer pair; pins 1 and 4 opposed, pins 2 and 3 opposed). Crank-speed balance shaft to cancel the primary rocking couple.
crank.note: Quotes (Yamaha feature copy on totalmotorcycle): 'locates the center two rods at a 90 degree plane from the outer cylinders ... they align on 2 planes in the form of a cross'; 'puts each connecting rod 90deg from the next'. Yamaha's own news release (https://global.yamaha-motor.com/news/2008/0909/yzf-r1.html): 'setting the interval between neighboring pistons at 1/4th of a revolution (90 degrees)'. The explicit 0, 90, 270, 180 pin sequence comes from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossplane): 'the throws may be described as being at absolute angles of 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees, versus the more usual 0, 90, 270, 180' (said of the Fath/URS engine versus the layout used 'in the Yamaha above'), image caption 'Crank throw orientation is up-left-right-down'. That sequence is consistent with the sourced firing order and intervals (see firing_intervals_deg). Sign convention (whether pin 2 leads or trails pin 1) is not stated; the interval derivation fixes it: cylinder 2 reaches TDC 90 degrees after cylinder 1, cylinder 4 180 after, cylinder 3 270 after. Balance shaft: Wikipedia, 'employing a crank-speed balance shaft to counter the inherent rocking vibration'; Yamaha copy calls it a 'coupling force balancer'.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Quoted figure: 'uneven firing interval of 270deg - 180deg - 90deg - 180deg' and 'fires 1,3,2,4 cylinders and the firing intervals are uneven at 270 / 180/ 90 /180 degrees'. Assignment to cylinders is DERIVED from that sentence read in order, not separately quoted: 1 fires, 270 later 3, 180 later 2, 90 later 4, 180 later 1 (sum 720). This is self-consistent with pins at 0/90/270/180: TDC phases cyl1 0, cyl2 90, cyl4 180, cyl3 270, giving fire times 0 (1), 270 (3), 450 (2), 540 (4). Wikipedia's Crossplane article lists the same cycle starting at a different point: 'firing intervals ... for the crossplane R1 and URS engines are 90-180-270-180 (crank degrees)'; that is the same sequence rotated, not a disagreement.

valves_per_cylinder.note: '4-valve DOHC'. Titanium intake valves, steel exhaust (Yamaha feature copy).

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: 2009 service manual: 'Valve head diameter A (intake)' 30.90-31.10 mm; value is the midpoint. Yamaha feature copy agrees: 'titanium intake valves are 31mm in diameter'. Read through a text extraction of the ManualsLib page (labels and values come out as separate lists and were paired by order), so spot-check against the page image.

exhaust_valve_dia_mm.note: 2009 service manual: 'Valve head diameter A (exhaust)' 24.90-25.10 mm; midpoint. Feature copy: 'steel exhaust valves are 25mm in diameter'. Read through a text extraction of the ManualsLib page (labels and values come out as separate lists and were paired by order), so spot-check against the page image.

valve_included_angle_deg.note: Feature copy: 'Steep valve angles, 11.5 degrees on the intake side and 12.5 degrees on the exhaust'. 24.0 is the sum (my arithmetic).

intake_lift_mm.note: No source states valve lift. Lobe height and base circle are in intake_cam_lobe_height_mm / intake_cam_base_circle_mm; their difference (about 9.3 mm, my arithmetic, before valve clearance; bucket tappets so roughly 1:1) is NOT a published lift.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: No source states valve lift. Lobe height minus base circle is about 8.4 mm (my arithmetic, before clearance); not a published lift.

intake_cam_lobe_height_mm.note: 2009 service manual, camshaft lobe dimensions: Intake A 37.350-37.450 mm (limit 37.250); midpoint recorded. This is LOBE HEIGHT, not valve lift. The page text does not say which letter is height and which is base circle; A is taken as lobe height because it is the larger dimension (inference). Same table on ?page=40.

intake_cam_base_circle_mm.note: Intake B 28.034-28.134 mm (limit 27.934); midpoint. Taken as base circle (the smaller dimension; inference).

exhaust_cam_lobe_height_mm.note: Exhaust A 36.450-36.550 mm (limit 36.350); midpoint. Lobe height, not lift.

exhaust_cam_base_circle_mm.note: Exhaust B 28.006-28.106 mm (limit 27.906); midpoint. Taken as base circle (inference).

valve_clearance_cold_mm.note: 2009 service manual, valve clearance (cold). The kit manual's STD column prints 0.11-0.20 / 0.21-0.25 (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/805484/Yamaha-Yzf-R1.html?page=5).

intake_lobe_centre_deg.note: WEAK READING. 2009 YZF-R1 racing kit manual (Yamaha Motor Engineering; parts prefixed 14B), 'Engine Specifications' table, row 'Valve timing (event angle)', columns SBK / STK / STD. The extracted text reads SBK 'INT. 108deg EXT. 110deg' then '103deg 105deg 103deg 105deg' for STK/STD. I read the pairs row-wise as STK 103 / STD 105 for intake and STK 103 / STD 105 for exhaust, because every other row pairs that way (CR 12.9:1 STK / 12.7:1 STD; squish 0.65 / 0.75). The alternative reading is STD intake 103, exhaust 105. 'Event angle' is taken to be the lobe centre angle (intake ATDC, exhaust BTDC); the manual does not define it on that page, and no lift is associated with it.

exhaust_lobe_centre_deg.note: Same table and same caveat as intake_lobe_centre_deg (105 in both readings).

intake_duration_deg.note: Not found; Yamaha manuals for this engine publish no opening/closing angles.

redline_rpm.note: 2010 YZF-R1 owner's manual (14B-28199-E2, same 14B generation): 'Red zone: 13750 r/min and above'. The 2009 kit manual gives the standard rev limiter as 13800 rpm ('Maximum engine speed (limiter controlled speed)', STD column, https://www.manualslib.com/manual/805484/Yamaha-Yzf-R1.html?page=5).

rev_limiter_rpm.note: 2009 racing kit manual, 'Maximum engine speed (limiter controlled speed)': 13800 rpm in all three columns (SBK, STK, STD).

idle_rpm.note: 2009 service manual: 'Engine idling speed 1150-1250 r/min'; midpoint recorded.

peak_power_kw.note: Yamaha news release, 2009 European model (excluding France): '133.9kW (182PS) / 12,500r/min'. Crank figure, quoted elsewhere by Yamaha as 'without air-induction' (ram air). Wikipedia's R1 article lists 191 hp (142 kW) @ 12,500 rpm 'without ram air' citing Yamaha's 2009 specs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamaha_YZF-R1); the Yamaha-hosted figure is used here.

peak_torque_nm.note: '115.5N.m (11.8kgf.m) / 10,000r/min'. The Canadian spec reproduced on totalmotorcycle gives 11.7 kg-m (84.6 ft-lb) @ 10,000 rpm, i.e. about 114.7 Nm (https://www.totalmotorcycle.com/photos/2009models/2009-Yamaha-YZFR1/).

intake_type.note: One 45 mm throttle per cylinder in a single throttle-body assembly (service manual type '45EIDW', quantity 1), ride-by-wire (YCC-T), primary injectors in the throttle bodies and secondary (showerhead) injectors in the airbox, ram-air fed airbox, variable-length funnels (YCC-I).

throttle_dia_mm.note: Yamaha feature copy: 'primary) are located in the 45mm throttle bodies'; Canadian spec table 'Mikuni 45mm throttle body FI'. 2009 service manual throttle body type '45EIDW' (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1080239/Yamaha-2009-Yzf-R1-Y.html?page=44) is consistent.

runner_length_mm.note: YCC-I funnel lengths (long and short) not found. The 2009 service manual's YCC-I feature pages describe the two positions without dimensions.

intake_funnel_switch_rpm.note: Yamaha feature copy: 'An electronic servo motor varies the funnel length from the tall position at low to mid rpms to the shorter setting for improved high rpm power. The transition rpm between the 2 lengths is approx. 9,400 rpms.' and 'It takes only 0.3 of a second for the funnels to move'. The service manual (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1080239/Yamaha-2009-Yzf-R1-Y.html?page=14) confirms long funnel low-to-mid rpm, short funnel high rpm, with no rpm figure; the ECU calculates funnel position, so treat 9,400 as approximate.

header_type.note: Yamaha news release: 'a 4-2-1-2 exhaust pipe and twin mufflers'. Feature copy: 'New 4 into 2 into 1 into 2 titanium exhaust system ... dual under seat mufflers'.

exhaust_notes.value: Titanium 4-2-1-2 system. EXUP titanium butterfly valve in the exhaust; 3-way honeycomb catalyser and oxygen sensor in the collector; twin short triangular under-seat mufflers of 'single expansion' type.
exhaust_notes.note: Yamaha feature copy: 'EXUP System (Exhaust Ultimate Power Valve) utilizes a titanium butterfly valve'; 'New dual shorty, large diameter triangle shaped mufflers are a "single expansion" type that create a throaty exhaust note'. Which primaries pair at the 4-2 junction is not stated; it matters for the sound and is listed as missing.

crank_journal_dia_mm.note: 'large 36mm diameter crank journal (compared to 32 mm on existing model)'; crank inertial moment 'increased by approx. 20%'.

cylinder_incline_deg.note: 'a 31-degree forward incline of the cylinders'. The feature copy on totalmotorcycle says '40 degree inclined'; the Yamaha-hosted release is preferred.

missing: cylinder numbering convention (which side is cylinder 1)
which header primaries pair at the 4-2 junction

sources.what: Yamaha Motor Co. news release of 2008-09-09 for the 2009 European YZF-R1: crossplane description, bore and stroke, compression, power, torque, 4-2-1-2 exhaust. Manufacturer primary source.

totalmotorcycle.com 2009 YZF-R1 page reproducing Yamaha's model feature copy and US/Canada/UK spec tables: firing order 1,3,2,4, intervals, valve sizes, 45 mm throttles, YCC-I switch rpm, exhaust and EXUP. Manufacturer text on a third-party page.
Yamaha 2009 YZF-R1 (Y) service manual on ManualsLib (547 pages): engine specifications pages 39-45, camshaft check page 263, YCC-I feature pages 13-16. Read page by page through text extraction.

Yamaha YZF-R1 racing kit manual on ManualsLib (92 pages, published by Yamaha Motor Engineering, parts prefixed 14B, so the 2009 kit): engine specification table with SBK/STK/STD columns (rev limit, compression, valve timing event angle).
Yamaha YZF-R1 2010 owner's manual (14B-28199-E2) on ManualsLib: tachometer red zone (page 25) and specifications (page 105).
Wikipedia, Crossplane: inline-four crossplane throw sequence and the R1's firing-interval cycle. Encyclopedia page; used only for the explicit pin sequence.
Wikipedia, Yamaha YZF-R1: generation table (alternative 191 hp power figure, 13,750 rpm rev limiter). Used for cross-checking only.

Yamaha 2020 YZF-R1 kit manual (the later 79.0 x 50.9 mm generation, NOT this engine): STD limiter 14500 rpm, compression 13.0, valve timing event angle INT 108 / EXT 110. Read for comparison when choosing the generation; no value above comes from it.

vehicle.name: Yamaha YZF-R1, 2009 (model code 14B, European specification)
vehicle.chosen_because: The engine definition is the 2009-2014 cross-plane R1 engine with 2009 data; the 2009 YZF-R1 is the bike that introduced it.

curb_kg.quote: Wet weight (with oil and full fuel tank) 206kg
curb_kg.note: Yamaha news release, 2009 European model. The 2009 service manual p2-1 agrees ('With oil and fuel 206 kg (454 lb)'). MOTORRAD measured 'Gewicht vollgetankt* 214 (210) kg' (https://www.motorradonline.de/supersportler/test-yamahas-neue-1000er-yamaha-yzf-r1-alt-gegen-neu/); Motorcyclist lists 474 lb for the 2010 US model.

gears.note: 2009 YZF-R1 service manual (14B1/14B2/14B3), p2-7, on ManualsLib; read through a helper's text-extraction tool (ManualsLib refuses direct downloads). The 2010 owner's manual (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/612261/Yamaha-Yzf-R1.html, pp.8-1/8-2) gives the same, and so does motorcyclespecs.co.za (https://www.motorcyclespecs.co.za/model/yamaha/yamaha_r1%2009.htm, a spec aggregator, corroboration only).

final_drive.quote: Primary reduction ratio 65/43 (1.512) ... Secondary reduction ratio 47/17 (2.765)
final_drive.note: My calculation: (65/43) x (47/17). The 2010 owner's manual agrees, and MOTORRAD gives 'Sekundärübersetzung 47:17 (45:17)' (45:17 is the 2008 bike).

wheel_radius_m.note: My calculation, not published: unloaded geometric radius from the nominal size (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio). The loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.

top_speed_kmh.quote: Höchstgeschwindigkeit (Herstellerangabe) Yamaha YZF-R1 2008 285 km/h Yamaha YZF-R1 2009 285 km/h
top_speed_kmh.note: Manufacturer's claim, printed by MOTORRAD (26.02.2009). Measured on a 2010 US R1 by Motorcyclist: 'a tested top speed of 176.7 mph' (284 km/h), https://www.motorcyclistonline.com/2010-yamaha-yzf-review/ (same generation, not checked by me).

sources.what: Yamaha Motor news release, 9 September 2008: 2009 European YZF-R1 main specifications.
Yamaha 2009 YZF-R1 service manual on ManualsLib (pp.2-1 to 2-9): weights, gearbox, reductions, tyres.
Yamaha 2010 YZF-R1 owner's manual (14B-28199-E2) on ManualsLib: same figures, cross-check.
MOTORRAD test 2009 vs 2008 R1, 26.02.2009: claimed top speed, measured weight, secondary ratio.
